title: State v. Imran
court: Addl. Sessions Judge-05 (Electricity), East, Karkardooma Courts, Delhi
result: Convicted u/s 135; civil liability (theft bill Rs. 11,61,828) settled and deposited; posted for sentence
statutes: Third proviso to Section 135(1) Electricity Act 2003

interpretations.interpretation: A wire hooked from the licensee's pole to unmetered premises powering a GSM antenna (telecom) tower is a clause (a) connection; partial seizure of the tapping wire (part out of reach) is not fatal — seizure is only corroborative where the theft is videographed. 'Dishonestly' takes its s.24 IPC meaning.

Reverse-onus clause: proof of an unauthorised means raises a compulsory presumption (Neeraj Dutt) rebuttable on the prudent-man standard (Hiten P. Dalal); natural rebuttal is paid bills / lawful metered use (s.106; Mukesh Rastogi).

citations.case: Punjab State Electricity Board v. Ashwani Kumar
citations.principle: An inspection report prepared by officers in discharge of official duty carries a presumption of regularity; onus on the consumer to rebut by cogent evidence.

citations.case: Sushil Sharma v. BSES Rajdhani Power Ltd.
citations.principle: Non-examination of an independent/public witness is no infirmity where inspecting officials are trustworthy and bear no enmity to the accused.
'Shall presume' denotes a compulsory legal presumption the court is bound to draw until the fact is disproved.

citations.case: Hiten P. Dalal v. Bratindranath Banerjee
citations.principle: Rebuttal of a statutory presumption need not be conclusive; evidence must make the defence reasonably probable to a prudent man.

citations.case: Mukesh Rastogi v. North Delhi Power Ltd.
citations.principle: Easiest rebuttal of the theft presumption is production of paid electricity bills; Section 106 Evidence Act places that onus on the consumer.

significance.point: Telecom/commercial loads drive the assessment sky-high
significance.explanation: Powering a GSM antenna tower (14.046 KW) produced a Rs. 11,61,828 bill — ~20x a domestic tap — because assessment follows the commercial tariff, doubled under Reg. 63.

significance.point: The accused's absence at inspection is no shield
significance.explanation: Family members identifying him as owner and user, plus his failure to deny it, fixed him as the consumer.

significance.point: Partial seizure of the wire is not fatal
significance.explanation: Where part of the tapping wire is out of reach, seizing the accessible segment suffices; seizure is only corroborative, the theft being videographed.

significance.point: A rooftop tower is not an innocent explanation
significance.explanation: That the load ran a functioning telecom tower confirmed a substantial, sustained abstraction rather than incidental domestic use.
Settling and depositing the very large theft bill was read as conduct inconsistent with innocence.

significance.point: The reverse-onus presumption did the rest
significance.explanation: No meter, unexplained running load, no Genset, no paid bills — the compulsory presumption convicted.

generic_facts.theft_mode: direct theft — pole hook (yellow wire from pole near transformer joined to black wire at balcony) powering a GSM antenna tower
generic_facts.occupant_at_inspection: accused absent; family members present identified accused as owner/user
generic_facts.ownership_evidence: family identified accused as owner/user; ownership documents seized
key_evidence: only accessible black wire seized (yellow wire too high)
generic_facts.defence: false implication; no defence evidence; settled + deposited theft bill
